Before, the set was split without subsets (`os.split(false)`), which never sets the principal member (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:419-428`), and since the team's `2fb7488717` (2012-05-09) nothing is written without one (`OverloadSet.java:2156-2157`): no such method existed in any component. Conditions: the checker leaves several declarations at a tie, as between a trait's functional method and that of an object that its `comprises` clause lists (rows 1100, 1112), and where a declaration is taken only by a coercion (row 390); the tie's order picks the call's arrow, either declaration's, from compile to compile (row 935). Evidence: `FunctionalMethodComprisedObject` (`num(R)`), `ComprisesSelfAbstractFunctionalMethodCall` (`s.total`, calls on `self`), `CoercionAnyOverloadRungC` (`p(NarrowOf(1))`), each red on the base with 'NoSuchMethodError: ... \=num{...}', '\=width{...}', '\=p{...}(fortress.AnyType$Any)', green on `7cf79900c2`; `ant testOneLibrary`, 'Tests run: 40, Failures: 0'. ## For FACTS

- **New entry. A compiled setter's call passes its value at the field's type, and a compiled call of several declarations names an overload method that the class holds.** The code generator passes the value of `c.t := v`, an arrowless call after the desugarer, at the setter's parameter type at the receiver's instance (`CodeGen.setterParamType`), cast below self's trait where it has self's type (F-377); it writes the overload method that a call names where the checker leaves it several declarations, its set split with its principal member (`CodeGen.for_RewriteFnOverloadDecl`), and, where the call's arrow is not the principal member's, a method at the call's signature that passes its arguments on (`CodeGen.forwardToPrincipal`). ## Revival change

**The change.** The team's code generator compiled an assignment to an object's `var` field, `c.t := v`, as a call of the field's setter at the value's static type, not the field's (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java`, `forMethodInvocation`, and the team's note there that such calls "don't have an OverloadingType", `:7498-7503`), so where the value's type is strictly below the field's the compiled program died with `NoSuchMethodError`.      2	component VarFieldAssignedSubtypeRun
     3	export Executable
     4	
     5	trait T
     6	    getter d(): ZZ32
     7	end
     8

    10	    getter d(): ZZ32 = 0
    11	end
    12	
    13	object High extends T
    14	    getter d(): ZZ32 = 2
    15	end
    16	
    17	object Cell(var t: T) end
    18	
    19	trait Q comprises { R }
    20	    putInto(s: Slot): () = do s.r := self end
    21	end
    22

    24	
    25	object Slot(var r: R) end

     3	export Executable
     4

    10	    depth(self): ZZ32
    11	    mass(self): ZZ32

    17	    depth(self): ZZ32 = d

    19	end
    20

     1	component CoercionAnyOverloadRungC
     2	export Executable
     3	
     4	(* An overloaded call that one declaration takes without coercion and another only by a coercion of its argument runs, compiled, the declaration that takes it without coercion (conversions-coercions.tex, section "Coercion Resolution"). *)
     5	
     6	trait Wide excludes { Narrow }
     7	  coerce(x: Narrow) = WideOf(x.small)
     8	  getter big(): ZZ32
     9	end
    10	trait Narrow excludes { Wide }
    11	  getter small(): ZZ32
    12	end
    13	object WideOf(b: ZZ32) extends Wide
    14	  getter big(): ZZ32 = b
    15	end
    16	object NarrowOf(s: ZZ32) extends Narrow
    17	  getter small(): ZZ32 = s
    18	end
    19	
    20	p(x: Wide): String = "p(Wide)"
    21	p(x: Any): String = "p(Any)"
    22	
    23	run(): () = do
    24	    println("REACHED")
    25	    assert(p(NarrowOf(1)), "p(Any)", "row 390: a declaration applicable without coercion is chosen; conversions-coercions.tex, section \"Coercion Resolution\"")

    27	end

Functional method declarations may be overloaded with top-level function
declarations.
----
we consider the declarations that are applicable to that call at run time.
If there is exactly one such declaration,
then the call dispatches to that declaration.
If there is no such declaration,
then the call is \emph{undefined}, which is a static error.
(However, see \secref{applicability-with-coercion}
for how coercion may add to the set of applicable declarations.)
If multiple declarations are applicable to the call at run time,
then we choose an arbitrary declaration among the declarations such that
no other applicable declaration is more specific than them.

== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

content.content:
\section{Subtype Rule}
\seclabel{subtype-rule}

If the parameter type of one declaration is a subtype of the parameter
type of another (and they are not the same) then there is no
ambiguity between these two declarations: for every call to which both
are applicable, the first is more specific.  This is the basis of the
Subtype Rule.

(* An assignment to a var field or through a setter, of a value whose static type is a strict subtype of the field's type, runs compiled: from outside the object, at a static parameter's instance, at a tuple type, at Any, through a trait's setter, on self in the object, through a receiver typed by a type variable, and of self at a type that its trait's comprises clause lists (bindings.tex, section "Assignments"). *)
object HCell(var h: T) extends Holder
    raise(): () = do self.h := High end
end

lift[\X extends Holder\](x: X): () = do x.h := High end

run(): () = do
    hd = HCell(Low)
    hd.raise()
    assert(hd.h.d, 2, "an assignment to self's field in the object's method")
    he = HCell(Low)
    lift[\HCell\](he)
    assert(he.h.d, 2, "an assignment through a receiver typed by a type variable")
    println("PASS")
  end

end

- problem: the planner's probes, compiled on the base, die with `NoSuchMethodError` at a setter's call and at an overload method (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-35/probes/fixes-35.md:46-47`)
- spec: assigning a field calls its setter, with a right-hand side of a subtype of the field's type (`Specification/basic/expressions/bindings.tex:60-61`, `:86-87`); a functional method is a top-level function overloaded with the others, and a call runs the most specific declaration applicable at run time (`Specification/basic/traits.tex:616-626`; `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:302-311`)

- deviation: a call at an arrow other than the principal member's gets a second method that passes its arguments on (`forwardToPrincipal`, `CodeGen.java:8723-8755`), which no other site writes; none from the specification's spelling
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java` (`CodeGen.java:7521-7527`, `:7728-7759`, `:8691-8755`)
